# Notation {.unnumbered}

Machine learning at scale sits at the convergence of three disciplines: machine learning, distributed systems, and high-performance data center networking. Training and serving modern foundation models requires orchestrating workloads across thousands of accelerators interconnected by high-speed networks. Each contributing field developed its mathematical conventions independently, creating severe symbol collisions when their concepts appear in the same system equation.

To a machine learning researcher, $B$ denotes batch size, while to a network engineer, $B$ denotes bandwidth. In distributed systems, $N$ represents the count of worker accelerators, whereas in statistics, $N$ denotes sample count. In high-performance computing, $P$ is commonly used for processor count, but in deep learning, $P$ is universally reserved for model parameter count. Similarly, in this book's communication models, $\alpha$ denotes per-message network latency and $\beta$ denotes link bandwidth, whereas in statistical learning, $\alpha$ represents a power-law scaling exponent and $\beta$ represents optimizer momentum.

This book establishes a rigorous, unified mathematical notation tailored specifically to distributed machine learning systems. The conventions defined below eliminate ambiguity across scaling laws, collective communication algorithms, parallel execution schedules, and cluster reliability models.

## The Governing Laws of Distributed Performance {#sec-notation-governing-laws .unlisted}

Performance modeling in distributed machine learning follows a natural two-tier hierarchy: the single-device execution foundation, and its fleet-wide composition.

### 1. The single-device foundation (the iron law of ML systems) {#sec-notation-conventions-iron-law-ml-systems-ce9d .unlisted}

Every distributed training step or inference pass is fundamentally composed of local execution on individual accelerators. For serialized execution phases on a single accelerator, the **iron law of ML Systems** decomposes execution time into memory access, arithmetic computation, and latency overhead:

$$\Time = \underbrace{\frac{\DataVolume}{\Bandwidth}}_{\text{Memory Time}} + \underbrace{\frac{\Operations}{\PeakRate \cdot \EfficiencyHw}}_{\text{Compute Time}} + \underbrace{\Latency}_{\text{Latency Overhead}}$$

Each symbol was chosen deliberately to preserve machine learning conventions while maintaining architectural precision:

::: {tbl-colwidths="[8,12,8,72]"}

| **Symbol**          | **Definition**     | **Unit** | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|:--------------------|:-------------------|:---------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\Time$**         | **Execution Time** | seconds  | Total serialized execution time in the iron-law performance decomposition.                                                                                                                                       |
| **$\Bandwidth$**    | **Bandwidth**      | bytes/s  | **Avoids collision with $\BatchSize$ (Batch Size)**. Systems literature often uses $B$ for bandwidth, while ML literature often uses $B$ for batch size. The notation preserves the ML convention.               |
| **$\DataVolume$**   | **Data Volume**    | bytes    | **Avoids collision with $\DatasetSize$ (Dataset Size)**. In scaling laws, $D$ means training tokens. Here we need bytes moved through memory. The subscript disambiguates.                                       |
| **$\EfficiencyHw$** | **Efficiency**     | —        | Hardware utilization $(0 \le \EfficiencyHw \le 1)$. Avoids collision with learning rate $(\LearningRate)$.                                                                                                       |
| **$\Latency$**      | **Latency**        | seconds  | **Avoids collision with $\Loss$ (Loss)**. Fixed overhead time (kernel launch, network RTT). The subscript distinguishes from the loss function.                                                                  |
| **$\Operations$**   | **Operations**     | FLOPs    | Total floating-point operations. Clean in equations (vs. "$\text{Ops}$").                                                                                                                                        |
| **$\PeakRate$**     | **Peak Rate**      | FLOP/s   | **Avoids collision with $\Parameters$ (Parameters)**. Roofline presentations often use $P$ for performance, while ML literature commonly uses $P$ for parameter count. The notation preserves the ML convention. |

:::

#### Why these choices matter {#sec-notation-conventions-choices-matter-0c16}

Without careful notation, statements about distributed systems become ambiguous:

> *"Reducing $D$ improves performance."*

In distributed machine learning, this could mean reducing the dataset size (fewer training samples), shrinking the data-parallel degree $\DataparallelDegreeDp$, or reducing the data volume $\DataVolume$ moved across the memory bus through quantization. With our notation, we distinguish them precisely:

> *"Reducing $\DataVolume$ through FP8 quantization cuts memory traffic across the interconnect while $\DatasetSize$ (training tokens) and $\DataparallelDegreeDp$ remain unchanged."*

#### Subscripted variants {#sec-notation-conventions-subscripted-variants}

The root symbol names the fundamental physical quantity, while an upright subscript specifies the precise domain or measurement point:

- $\Bandwidth_{\text{memory}}$, $\Bandwidth_{\text{network}}$, $\Bandwidth_{\text{interconnect}}$: bandwidth across distinct tiers of the distributed memory and fabric hierarchy.
- $\DataVolume$, $\PeakRate$, $\Latency$, $\EfficiencyHw$: single-node iron-law terms, held clear of shared ML symbols.
- $\EnergyPerByteMoved$, $\EnergyPerOperationCompute$, $\TotalEnergy$: energy budget components across distributed compute nodes.

The subscript therefore carries part of the claim. Memory and network bandwidth differ by orders of magnitude, so a figure is reproducible only when the subscript says where it was measured.

### 2. The Fleet Law (distributed step time) {#sec-notation-distributed}

When scaling a model across a fleet of $N = \AcceleratorCount$ accelerators, single-device compute time is distributed across workers, while communication and synchronization overheads are introduced. Under partitioned execution of fixed work, the governing equation is the **Fleet Law** (the distributed step time law, @eq-fleet-law):

$$\DistributedStepTime = \frac{\IronlawTermTimesCompute}{N} + \CommunicationTime + \SynchronizationTime - \OverlappedTime$$

| **Symbol**                                              | **Definition**                        | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                           |
|:--------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|:--------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\NumberOfDevices, \AcceleratorCount$**               | **Number of Devices**                 | Integer       | Accelerator count in a distributed job, the core's $\AcceleratorCount$ ($N = \AcceleratorCount$); also the rank count of a collective. *(Not parameters, use $P$.)* |
| **$\AcceleratorsPerNode$, $\AcceleratorsPerNodeNodes$** | **Accelerators per Node, Node Count** | Integer       | Hierarchical collectives split the fleet as $N = \AcceleratorsPerNode \AcceleratorsPerNodeNodes$. *(Bare $G$ is the LogGP gap per byte.)*                           |
| **$\DistributedStepTime$**                              | **Distributed Step Time**             | seconds       | Wall-clock time for one training step at scale $N$.                                                                                                                 |
| **$\IronlawTermTimesCompute$**                          | **Single-Device Compute Time**        | seconds       | The core's compute term for one training step (forward + backward pass) on one device.                                                                              |
| **$\CommunicationTime$**                                | **Communication Time**                | seconds       | Time for collective operations (AllReduce, AllGather); depends on payload, topology, and $N$.                                                                       |
| **$\OverlappedTime$**                                   | **Overlapped Time**                   | seconds       | Communication hidden behind computation. Reduces effective overhead.                                                                                                |
| **$\SynchronizationTime$**                              | **Synchronization Time**              | seconds       | Total nonoverlapped synchronization or coordination cost per step at scale $N$.                                                                                     |
| **$\rho$**                                              | **Communication-Computation Ratio**   | Dimensionless | $\rho = \CommunicationTime/(\IronlawTermTimesCompute/N)$. Values near or above 1 indicate communication-bound scaling.                                              |
| **$\CommunicationIntensity$**                           | **Communication Intensity**           | bytes/FLOP    | Network bytes moved per local FLOP, $\CommunicationIntensity = M/O$; the fleet analogue of arithmetic intensity $I$.                                                |

### 3. Scaling laws of foundation models {#sec-notation-scaling-laws}

Scaling laws anchor the book's account of why machine learning moved onto fleets. The single-resource power law and the dense-transformer compute rule are:

$$\mathcal{L}(X) = \ScaleCoefficient X^{-\ScalingExponentScale} + \IrreducibleLoss, \qquad \TrainingCompute \approx 6PD$$

| **Symbol**                  | **Definition**        | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                           |
|:----------------------------|:----------------------|:--------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$X$**                     | **Scaled Resource**   | varies        | Training compute, parameter count $P$, or training tokens $D$, depending on the fitted law.                         |
| **$\ScalingExponentScale$** | **Scaling Exponent**  | Dimensionless | Fitted power-law exponent; valid only within the regime in which it was measured. *(Not network latency $\alpha$.)* |
| **$\ScaleCoefficient$**     | **Scale Coefficient** | loss units    | Task-dependent fitted constant.                                                                                     |
| **$\IrreducibleLoss$**      | **Irreducible Loss**  | loss units    | Loss floor that added resources do not remove within the fitted regime.                                             |
| **$\TrainingCompute$**      | **Training Compute**  | FLOPs         | About $6PD$ for a dense transformer: $2P$ per token forward and $4P$ backward.                                      |

### 4. The distributed energy corollary {#sec-notation-conventions-energy-corollary-a1da .unlisted}

At data center scale, energy and power delivery are primary system constraints. For $N$ devices that each move the same $\DataVolume$ bytes and execute the same $\Operations$ FLOPs over a workload interval, effective per-byte data-movement costs and per-operation compute costs give the following fleet energy model. Here the work and traffic terms are per-device quantities, so multiplying by $N$ sums the device contributions:

$$\TotalEnergy \approx N \times \left( \DataVolume \times \EnergyPerByteMoved + \Operations \times \EnergyPerOperationCompute \right)$$

::: {tbl-colwidths="[10,25,15,50]"}

| **Symbol**                       | **Definition**            | **Unit**    | **Notes**                                                                                  |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------|:------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\EnergyPerByteMoved$**        | **Energy per Byte Moved** | joules/byte | Effective movement cost; total energy also depends on bytes moved and operations executed. |
| **$\EnergyPerOperationCompute$** | **Energy per Operation**  | joules/FLOP | Energy cost of a single arithmetic operation.                                              |
| **$\TotalEnergy$**               | **Total Energy**          | joules      | Total energy consumed by an ML workload, decomposed into data-movement and compute terms.  |

:::

## Network Communication Models and Collectives {#sec-notation-comm-models}

Collective communications (AllReduce, AllGather, ReduceScatter, AllToAll) transfer payloads across network fabrics structured as rings, trees, or fat-tree fabrics.

### The \texorpdfstring{$\alpha$-$\beta$}{alpha-beta} communication model {#sec-notation-alpha-beta}

Network communication time decomposes into fixed message startup latency and bandwidth-dependent transfer:

$$T(n) = \alpha + \frac{n}{\beta}$$

The model keeps its literature's letters as aliases of core concepts: $\alpha$ is the per-message $\Latency$ and $\beta$ is a link's $\Bandwidth$, written in $\alpha$-$\beta$ form. Inside $\alpha$-$\beta$ formulas, write $\alpha$ and $\beta$; elsewhere, write $\Latency$ and a subscripted $\Bandwidth$.

| **Symbol**                                                           | **Definition**                   | **Unit** | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|:---------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------|:---------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$T(n)$**                                                           | **Point-to-Point Transfer Time** | seconds  | Wall-clock time to transmit one message of size $n$ across one link.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **$n$**                                                              | **Point-to-Point Message Size**  | bytes    | Size of one message in $T(n)$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **$\alpha$**                                                         | **Per-Message Latency**          | seconds  | The core's $\Latency$ for one message, in $\alpha$-$\beta$ form: the fixed startup cost. *(Not significance level or Rényi order, which carry subscripts.)*                                                                                                                  |
| **$\beta$**                                                          | **Link Bandwidth**               | bytes/s  | The core's $\Bandwidth$ for one link ($\Bandwidth_{\text{link}}$), in $\alpha$-$\beta$ form: effective throughput per link.                                                                                                                                                  |
| **$\CrossoverPoint$**                                                | **Crossover Point**              | bytes    | $n^* = \alpha \cdot \beta$. Below $n^*$: latency-bound. Above: bandwidth-bound.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **$M$**                                                              | **Collective Payload Size**      | bytes    | Per-rank gradient, model-state, activation, or compressed payload that a collective moves. Not a memory footprint (those are $\TotalMemoryFootprint$, $\WeightMemoryWeights$, and so on) and not the core's GEMM dimension $M$, which appears only in GEMM shape statements. |
| **$\CollectiveCompletionTimeRing$, $\CollectiveCompletionTimeTree$** | **Collective Completion Time**   | seconds  | AllReduce time under the ring or tree algorithm in $\alpha$-$\beta$ form, for example $\CollectiveCompletionTimeRing = 2(N-1)\alpha + 2\frac{N-1}{N}\frac{M}{\beta}$. $T_{\text{allreduce}}$ names an AllReduce whose algorithm the text leaves open.                        |
| **$\RingtreeCrossoverPayload$**                                      | **Ring-Tree Crossover Payload**  | bytes    | Payload at which $\CollectiveCompletionTimeRing = \CollectiveCompletionTimeTree$; approximately $N\alpha\beta/\log_2 N$ for large $N$.                                                                                                                                       |

### The LogGP extension {#sec-notation-loggp}

LogGP refines the $\alpha$-$\beta$ model by separating network transit latency, processor initiation overhead, and long-message injection gaps. The book uses descriptive subscripts for the highest-collision terms; the bare letters $g$ and $G$ keep their LogGP meanings inside this model only.

| **Symbol**                     | **Definition**                 | **Unit**     | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------|:-------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\LoggpLongmessageTime$**    | **LogGP Long-Message Time**    | seconds      | Transfer time for an $n$-byte long message. Reuses $n$ from the $\alpha$-$\beta$ model.                                                                                                                                                    |
| **$\LogploggpNetworkLatency$** | **LogP/LogGP Network Latency** | seconds      | Network transit time of one message, the part of the core's $\Latency$ that excludes processor overhead, so $\alpha \approx \SenderOverhead + \LogploggpNetworkLatency + \ReceiverOverheadRecv$. The subscript avoids bare $L$ collisions. |
| **$\SenderOverhead$**          | **Sender Overhead**            | seconds      | Processor/NIC overhead to initiate a message.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **$\ReceiverOverheadRecv$**    | **Receiver Overhead**          | seconds      | Processor/NIC overhead to complete a message. Symmetric LogP writes $o = \SenderOverhead = \ReceiverOverheadRecv$, so one message costs $2o$.                                                                                              |
| **$g$**                        | **Message Injection Gap**      | seconds      | Minimum interval between consecutive message injections. *(Gradients are bold, $\mathbf{g}$.)*                                                                                                                                             |
| **$G$**                        | **Long-Message Gap per Byte**  | seconds/byte | Per-byte long-message gap; distinct from $\beta$ link bandwidth. *(Accelerators per node are $\AcceleratorsPerNode$.)*                                                                                                                     |

### Compression economics {#sec-notation-compression-economics}

Compression models compare codec overhead against the communication time saved by reducing payload size:

| **Symbol**                         | **Definition**                    | **Unit** | **Notes**                                                                                         |
|:-----------------------------------|:----------------------------------|:---------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$T_{\text{transfer}}(x)$**       | **Transfer Time for Payload $x$** | seconds  | Communication time for an $x$-byte payload: $T(x)$ for one link, or the relevant collective time. |
| **$\CompressedCommunicationTime$** | **Compressed Communication Time** | seconds  | Total time after encode, transfer of $M/\CompressionRatio$, and decode.                           |
| **$\CodecEncodeTime$**             | **Codec Encode Time**             | seconds  | Local compression overhead before transfer.                                                       |
| **$\CodecDecodeTime$**             | **Codec Decode Time**             | seconds  | Local decompression overhead after transfer.                                                      |

## Parallelism Dimensions and Scaling Efficiency {#sec-notation-parallelism-scaling}

Scaling large foundation models requires combining multiple parallelism strategies across device dimensions.

### Parallelism dimensions {#sec-notation-parallelism}

3D parallelism partitions the training workload across three orthogonal dimensions:

$$N = \DataparallelDegreeDp \times \PipelineparallelDegreePp \times \TensorparallelDegreeTp$$

| **Symbol**                            | **Definition**                         | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                      |
|:--------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------|:--------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\DataparallelDegreeDp$**           | **Data-Parallel Degree**               | Integer       | Number of model replicas. *(Bare $d$ stays the core's hidden dimension.)*                                                                                      |
| **$\PipelineparallelDegreePp$**       | **Pipeline-Parallel Degree**           | Integer       | Number of physical pipeline stages in model-depth partitioning.                                                                                                |
| **$\TensorparallelDegreeTp$**         | **Tensor-Parallel Degree**             | Integer       | Degree of intra-layer partitioning (model width). *(Bare $t$ stays time or a step index.)*                                                                     |
| **$m$**                               | **Microbatch Count**                   | Integer       | Number of microbatches used to fill and drain the pipeline.                                                                                                    |
| **$\PipelineBubbleFraction$**         | **Pipeline Bubble Fraction**           | Dimensionless | Fraction of pipeline GPU-time spent idle, $\PipelineBubbleFraction = (\PipelineparallelDegreePp-1)/(\PipelineparallelDegreePp-1+m)$; avoids bare $b$.          |
| **$\VirtualPipelineStagesPerDevice$** | **Virtual Pipeline Stages per Device** | Integer       | Number of interleaved virtual chunks assigned to each physical pipeline stage. *(The attention value matrix is bold, $\mathbf{V}$.)*                           |
| **$\GradientStaleness$**              | **Gradient Staleness**                 | steps         | Number of parameter updates between the parameters a gradient was computed on and the parameters it updates; $\GradientStaleness = 0$ is synchronous training. |

### Scaling efficiency {#sec-notation-scaling}

Scaling efficiency measures realized speedup relative to ideal linear scaling:

$$\ScalingEfficiency = \frac{T_1}{N \times T_N}$$

| **Symbol**                 | **Definition**         | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                              |
|:---------------------------|:-----------------------|:--------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\ScalingEfficiency$**   | **Scaling Efficiency** | Dimensionless | Ratio of measured speedup to ideal linear speedup. $1.0$ is the ideal linear baseline, not a hard upper bound.         |
| **$\SingledeviceTimeOne$** | **Single-Device Time** | seconds       | Baseline wall-clock time for the same productive work on one device.                                                   |
| **$\NdeviceTime$**         | **N-Device Time**      | seconds       | Wall-clock time for the same productive work on $N$ devices; excludes operational downtime counted by $\GoodputRatio$. |

## Cluster Reliability, Fault Tolerance, and Checkpointing {#sec-notation-reliability-sec}

At cluster scale, hardware component failures are standard operating conditions rather than rare anomalies.

### Fault tolerance and reliability {#sec-notation-reliability}

Assuming independent components with exponential failure distributions, system reliability across $N$ components is:

$$\ReliabilityFunctionSystem = e^{-N\lambda t}$$

The aggregate exponent uses the system-level rate $N\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the per-component failure rate under the independent, identical-component assumption. The exponent $N\lambda t$ is dimensionless, so the elapsed time $t$ must use the same time unit as $\lambda$ (hours, when $\lambda$ comes from the FIT-derived rates below).

The optimal checkpoint interval balances I/O overhead against recomputation rework:

$$\OptimalCheckpointIntervalCkpt = \sqrt{2 \cdot \CheckpointWriteTime \cdot \MeanTimeBetweenFailures_{\text{system}}}$$

The formula uses the *system-wide* mean time between failures (the failure interval for the whole job), not a *component* lifetime; substituting the per-component value would overestimate $\OptimalCheckpointIntervalCkpt$ by $\sqrt{N}$. For dimensional consistency, $\CheckpointWriteTime$ and $\MeanTimeBetweenFailures_{\text{system}}$ must be in the same time unit. Industry-standard $\MeanTimeBetweenFailures$ is reported in hours; to combine it with seconds-scale write times, multiply the hour value by 3600. The result $\OptimalCheckpointIntervalCkpt$ then carries the time unit chosen for the inputs.

| **Symbol**                           | **Definition**                  | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|:-------------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:--------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\ReliabilityFunctionSystem$**     | **Reliability Function**        | Probability   | Probability of no failure across the whole system before time $t$. One component has $R_{\text{single}}(t) = e^{-\lambda t}$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **$\lambda$**                        | **Per-Component Failure Rate**  | failures/hour | Per-component failure rate, written $\lambda_{\text{fail}}$ wherever another rate shares the passage; the system-wide rate is $N\lambda$ under independent, identical components. The industry-standard reporting unit is FIT (failures per $10^9$ device-hours): $\lambda_{\text{hour}} = \text{FIT} \times 10^{-9}$. *(Other rates carry subscripts, such as the core's arrival rate $\ArrivalRate$.)* |
| **$\MeanTimeBetweenFailures$**       | **Mean Time Between Failures**  | hours         | Average time between consecutive failures of a repairable, composed system. $\MeanTimeBetweenFailures_{\text{system}} = 1/(N\lambda) = \MeanTimeToFailure_{\text{component}} / N$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **$\MeanTimeToFailure$**             | **Mean Time To Failure**        | hours         | Per-component lifetime constant derived from FIT rates, $\MeanTimeToFailure_{\text{component}} = 1/\lambda$. Distinct from system-level $\MeanTimeBetweenFailures$ when repair/replacement cycles are modeled.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **$\MeanTimeToRepair$**              | **Mean Time To Repair**         | hours         | Average recovery time after a failure.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **$\CheckpointIntervalCkpt$**        | **Checkpoint Interval**         | seconds       | Useful compute time between consecutive checkpoints.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **$\OptimalCheckpointIntervalCkpt$** | **Optimal Checkpoint Interval** | seconds       | The $\CheckpointIntervalCkpt$ that minimizes total wasted time; Young-Daly formula.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\CheckpointWriteTime$**           | **Checkpoint Write Time**       | seconds       | Time to persist model state to storage.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### Fleet capacity factors and goodput {#sec-notation-fleet-capacity}

Fleet capacity metrics compound model arithmetic efficiency, scaling efficiency, and operational goodput:

| **Symbol**                                                                                                                    | **Definition**                      | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------|:--------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\UsefulComputetimeFraction$**                                                                                              | **Useful Compute-Time Fraction**    | Dimensionless | $(\IronlawTermTimesCompute/N)/\DistributedStepTime$. Measures how much step time is useful local arithmetic after distribution.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **$\OperationalOverheadFraction$**                                                                                            | **Operational Overhead Fraction**   | Dimensionless | Fraction of allocated wall time lost outside the productive steps measured by $T_N$, such as checkpoint pauses, failure recovery, scheduler preemption, or maintenance.                                                                                                                                                             |
| **$\GoodputRatio$**                                                                                                           | **Goodput Ratio**                   | Dimensionless | Fraction of allocated wall time remaining after the out-of-step losses in $\OperationalOverheadFraction$; often $\GoodputRatio = 1 - \OperationalOverheadFraction$.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **$\EffectiveFleetThroughput$**                                                                                               | **Effective Fleet Throughput**      | FLOP/s        | $\EffectiveFleetThroughput = (N \PeakRate) \times \ModelFlopsUtilization \times \ScalingEfficiency \times \GoodputRatio$, where $\ModelFlopsUtilization$ is the single-device baseline, $\ScalingEfficiency$ captures all in-step scaling loss, and $\GoodputRatio$ captures only out-of-step operational loss excluded from $T_N$. |
| **$\UsefulModelFlops$**                                                                                                       | **Useful Model FLOPs**              | FLOPs         | Model FLOPs that advance training, excluding recomputation and padding; $\ModelFlopsUtilization = \UsefulModelFlops/(N \PeakRate T_{\text{step}})$ measures fleet MFU and already includes in-step scaling loss. The throughput factorization uses single-device baseline MFU instead.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **$\MlProductivityGoodputFactorsProgram$, $\MlProductivityGoodputFactorsRuntime$, $\MlProductivityGoodputFactorsScheduling$** | **ML Productivity Goodput Factors** | Dimensionless | Program, runtime, and scheduling goodput, with $\text{MPG} = \MlProductivityGoodputFactorsScheduling \times \MlProductivityGoodputFactorsRuntime \times \MlProductivityGoodputFactorsProgram$. A complementary lifecycle decomposition, not a factorization of $\EffectiveFleetThroughput$.                                         |
| **$\FleetEnergyProductivity$**                                                                                                | **Fleet Energy Productivity**       | FLOP/J        | Useful computation per unit energy, $\UsefulModelFlops$ divided by the energy drawn inside the stated boundary.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **$\DollarCostTrain$, $\DollarCostInfer$**                                                                                    | **Dollar Cost**                     | dollars       | The subscript names the cost component. Carbon quantities use $\text{CO}_{2,\dots}$, never $C$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Distributed Memory Hierarchy and Serving at Scale {#sec-notation-memory-serving}

Managing distributed memory requires partitioning weights, activations, optimizer states, and KV-cache tensors across nodes and tiers.

### Distributed memory and serving metrics {#sec-notation-conventions-performance-serving-memory .unlisted}

Reusable performance and serving quantities follow the same collision-avoidance rule as the iron law. Rates use $R$ or descriptive Greek symbols; request counts use $\RequestConcurrency$ rather than overloading $N$; queue utilization uses a subscripted $\rho$ so bare $\rho$ remains available for other ratio models.

```{=latex}
\begingroup
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
```
::: {tbl-colwidths="[10,23,13,54]"}

| **Symbol**                      | **Definition**                 | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|:--------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\ActivationMemory$**         | **Activation Memory**          | bytes         | Retained activations for the backward pass or serving intermediates.                                                                                                                                                    |
| **$\ArrivalRate$**              | **Arrival Rate**               | requests/s    | Request arrival rate. The subscript keeps bare $\lambda$ free for fitted sensitivities.                                                                                                                                 |
| **$\AttainableComputeRate$**    | **Attainable Compute Rate**    | FLOP/s        | Roofline bound: $\AttainableComputeRate \leq \min(\PeakRate, I \times \Bandwidth)$. Uses $R$, not $T$, because this quantity is a rate.                                                                                 |
| **$\BatchServiceTime$**         | **Batch Service Time**         | seconds       | Time to serve a batch of size $B$.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\CompressionRatio$**         | **Compression Ratio**          | Dimensionless | Uncompressed size divided by compressed size. A compressed payload has $1/\CompressionRatio$ of the uncompressed size; the subscript avoids bare $C$ collisions.                                                        |
| **$\EffectiveServiceRate$**     | **Effective Service Rate**     | requests/s    | Batched service rate, typically $\EffectiveServiceRate = B/\BatchServiceTime$. The unbatched service rate is $\mu = \mu_{\text{eff}}(1)$.                                                                               |
| **$\ElementStorageSize$**       | **Element Storage Size**       | bytes/element | Bytes per stored tensor element.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **$\GradientMemory$**           | **Gradient Memory**            | bytes         | Memory occupied by stored gradients.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **$\ModelFlopsUtilization$**    | **Model FLOPs Utilization**    | Dimensionless | Useful model FLOP/s divided by available peak FLOP/s. Text acronym avoids overloading $\eta$.                                                                                                                           |
| **$\OptimizerstateMemory$**     | **Optimizer-State Memory**     | bytes         | Momentum, variance, master weights, and related optimizer buffers.                                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\RequestConcurrency$**       | **Request Concurrency**        | requests      | Average in-flight requests in a stable serving system ($\RequestConcurrency = \ArrivalRate \cdot \RequestTimeInSystem$ via Little's Law). Avoids overloading $N$, which counts devices, elements, or samples elsewhere. |
| **$\RequestTimeInSystem$**      | **Request Time in System**     | seconds       | End-to-end queueing/serving latency for Little's Law. Distinct from $\Latency$, the fixed-latency term in the iron law.                                                                                                 |
| **$I$**                         | **Arithmetic Intensity**       | FLOP/byte     | Workload FLOPs per byte moved. The roofline model uses $I$ as the independent variable.                                                                                                                                 |
| **$\RooflineRidgePoint$**       | **Roofline Ridge Point**       | FLOP/byte     | $\RooflineRidgePoint = \PeakRate/\Bandwidth$. Prefer this explicit form over starred shorthand so the meaning remains clear in prose.                                                                                   |
| **$\ServingUtilization$**       | **Serving Utilization**        | Dimensionless | Queue/server utilization. The subscript keeps bare $\rho$ free for other ratio models.                                                                                                                                  |
| **$\TotalMemoryFootprint$**     | **Total Memory Footprint**     | bytes         | Sum of explicit memory components; avoids bare $M$ ambiguity; the core's quantity.                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\WeightMemory$**             | **Weight Memory**              | bytes         | Memory occupied by model weights ($P \times \text{bytes-per-parameter}$); the core's quantity.                                                                                                                          |
| **$\SustainedMemoryBandwidth$** | **Sustained Memory Bandwidth** | bytes/s       | Empirically achievable memory bandwidth under target access patterns.                                                                                                                                                   |

:::


### Serving memory at scale {#sec-notation-serving-memory-scale}

| **Symbol**                  | **Definition**               | **Unit**    | **Notes**                                                                                                                                 |
|:----------------------------|:-----------------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\KvcacheMemory$**        | **KV-Cache Memory**          | bytes       | Total key-value cache footprint for autoregressive serving, $\KvcacheMemory = B \cdot S \cdot \KvcacheBytesPerToken$.                     |
| **$\KvcacheBytesPerToken$** | **KV-Cache Bytes per Token** | bytes/token | $\KvcacheBytesPerToken = 2 N_L \NumberOfKeyvalueHeadsKv \AttentionHeadDimension \ElementStorageSize$ (keys and values across all layers). |

## Deep Learning Foundations in Distributed Contexts {#sec-notation-conventions-deep-learning-notation-b40d .unlisted}

Distributed algorithms partition neural architectures defined by standard deep learning conventions [@goodfellow2016deep]:

::: {tbl-colwidths="[18,22,12,48]"}

| **Symbol**                                            | **Definition**                | **Unit**                        | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                 |
|:------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$d$**                                               | **Hidden Dimension**          | Integer                         | Size of the hidden state vector. *(Parallelism degrees carry subscripts, such as $\DataparallelDegreeDp$.)*                                                               |
| **$\AttentionHeadDimension$**                         | **Attention Head Dimension**  | Integer                         | Per-head hidden dimension in attention layers.                                                                                                                            |
| **$\LayerInputWidth$**                                | **Layer Input Width**         | Integer                         | Number of input features in a layer.                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\LayerOutputWidth$**                               | **Layer Output Width**        | Integer                         | Number of output features in a layer.                                                                                                                                     |
| **$\ModelParameters$**                                | **Model Parameters**          | Vector                          | Trainable model weight and bias parameter vector $\theta$.                                                                                                                |
| **$\Policy$**                                         | **Policy**                    | Function                        | Target neural network policy $\pi_\theta(a \mid s)$.                                                                                                                      |
| **$S$**                                               | **Sequence Length**           | Integer                         | Input context or sequence length $S$ in tokens.                                                                                                                           |
| **$\ell$**                                            | **Layer Index**               | Integer                         | Index for a layer. Use instead of bare $L$ when indexing layers, since $L$ collides with loss and latency. A numeric subscript marks a norm instead ($\ell_1$, $\ell_2$). |
| **$\LossFunction$**                                   | **Loss Function**             | Scalar                          | The objective function minimized during training.                                                                                                                         |
| **$\NumberOfAttentionHeads, \NumberOfKeyValueHeads$** | **Number of Attention Heads** | Integer                         | Number of attention heads in a multi-head attention layer, and key-value heads $H_{\text{KV}}$ (in GQA/MQA).                                                              |
| **$\NumberOfLayers$**                                 | **Number of Layers**          | Integer                         | Total number of layers in a network.                                                                                                                                      |
| **$p(x)$**                                            | **Distribution**              | Probability mass/density        | Use lowercase $p(\cdot)$ for generic distributions to avoid collision with $P$ (parameter count).                                                                         |
| **$p(y \mid x)$**                                     | **Conditional Distribution**  | Conditional probability/density | Use this form for generic label relationships.                                                                                                                            |
| **$\Pr(E)$**                                          | **Event Probability**         | Probability                     | Probability of an event $E$, as in $\Pr(\text{batch}=0)$; use $p(x)$ and $p(y \mid x)$ for distributions.                                                                 |

:::

Latin matrices and vectors are set in bold ($\mathbf{W}$, $\mathbf{x}$); scalars, dimensions, indices, and individual matrix entries stay italic ($N$, $d$, $i$, $W_{ij}$). The generic parameter symbol $\theta$ is the conventional exception and stays italic. Matrix operands in general matrix multiply (GEMM) are bold ($\mathbf{C} = \alpha \mathbf{A}\mathbf{B} + \beta \mathbf{C}$), distinct from the scalar batch size $B$. GEMM dimensions are $M$, $N$, and $K$. Asymptotic complexity is written $\mathcal{O}(\cdot)$, distinct from total operations $O$.

## Privacy, Robustness, Governance, and Distributed Constants {#sec-notation-governance}

Federated systems, distributed coordination, and cluster operations rely on standardized metrics:

### Privacy, robustness, and statistical testing {#sec-notation-privacy-robustness}

Part IV uses the standard symbols of differential privacy and adversarial robustness, and the operations and robustness chapters use those of hypothesis testing. The same Greek letters appear in several of these fields, so every use other than the one named below carries a subscript.

| **Symbol**                                                          | **Definition**                      | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                                             |
|:--------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------|:--------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$(\epsilon, \delta)$**                                            | **Differential Privacy Budget**     | Dimensionless | $\epsilon$ bounds the privacy loss from adding or removing one protected record; $\delta$ is the allowed failure probability.         |
| **$\AdversarialPerturbationBudget$**                                | **Adversarial Perturbation Budget** | input units   | Radius of the allowed input perturbation under a stated norm. *(Not the privacy budget $\epsilon$.)*                                  |
| **$\AttackStepsPgd$**                                               | **Attack Steps**                    | Integer       | Inner iterations of a projected gradient descent (PGD) attack; adversarial training costs about $\AttackStepsPgd+1$ passes per batch. |
| **$\TypeIAndTypeIiErrorRatesSig$, $\TypeIAndTypeIiErrorRatesStat$** | **Type I and Type II Error Rates**  | Probability   | Significance level and miss rate of a hypothesis test; statistical power is $1-\TypeIAndTypeIiErrorRatesStat$.                        |
| **$\mathbb{E}[\cdot]$**                                             | **Expectation**                     | —             | Expected value. Blackboard bold keeps it distinct from an event $E$ and the energy terms such as $\TotalEnergy$.                      |

### Distributed governance, reliability, and safety constants {#sec-notation-governance-constants .unlisted}

::: {tbl-colwidths="[10,23,13,54]"}

| **Symbol**                           | **Definition**                  | **Unit** | **Notes**                                                                                                                                      |
|:-------------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:---------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$h(x)$**                           | **Classifier**                  | Function | Binary classifier $h(x)$ whose positive-prediction rates the fairness criteria constrain.                                                      |
| **$C$**                              | **Gradient Clipping Norm**      | Scalar   | Per-example gradient clipping bound $C$ in differentially private training; not a C$^3$ axis.                                                  |
| **$\Deadline$**                      | **Deadline**                    | seconds  | Target latency deadline for batch or phase completion.                                                                                         |
| **$\HandoverTimeout$**               | **Failure-Detection Timeout**   | seconds  | Interval without a heartbeat after which the coordinator declares a rank failed.                                                               |
| **$\ResponseThreshold$**             | **Response Threshold**          | Scalar   | Decision or classification threshold $\tau$.                                                                                                   |
| **$\SequentialLoglikelihoodRatioM$** | **Sequential Likelihood Ratio** | Scalar   | Likelihood ratio $\Lambda_m$ after $m$ observations in sequential probability ratio testing (SPRT), compared against Wald stopping boundaries. |

:::

## Units, Precision, and Disambiguation {#sec-notation-units-disambiguation}

Standardized measurement units, numerical representation formats, and collision-avoidance conventions ensure clarity across distributed systems analysis.

### Units and precision {#sec-notation-conventions-units-precision-fdaf .unlisted}

*   Physical units: This book uses SI (metric) units throughout, including meters, kilograms, seconds, watts, and °C, consistent with standard engineering and scientific practice. Where source data was originally reported in imperial units, the book converts to SI and notes the original values parenthetically. A space always separates the number from the unit (for example, 100 ms, 2 TB/s).
*   Data and memory: This book uses **decimal SI prefixes only**: KB = $10^3$ bytes, MB = $10^6$, GB = $10^9$, TB = $10^{12}$. Binary-prefixed units do not appear in prose; model sizes, activation footprints, throughputs, and transfer volumes are reported in decimal units (for example, 2 TB/s, 102 MB). Hardware memory capacities retain the vendor's nameplate figure and label. A modeled capacity of $80 \times 2^{30}$ bytes follows the registered device assumption, not a guarantee implied by an 80 GB label. Where a worked example subtracts a computed footprint from a device capacity, the registered capacity in bytes and the footprint are both converted to decimal; @sec-appdx-fleet-system-assumptions states this exception in full.
*   Compute: The notation distinguishes operation counts from rates. Total work uses FLOPs (for example, GFLOPs, TFLOPs), while throughput uses FLOP/s with decimal prefixes (for example, GFLOP/s, TFLOP/s).
    *   1 TFLOP = $10^{12}$ FLOPs
    *   1 TFLOP/s = $10^{12}$ FLOPs per second
    *   Arithmetic intensity conventionally uses FLOP/byte as a unit ratio (floating-point operations per byte moved).
*   Network throughput: Reported in bytes/s (GB/s, TB/s) or bits/s (Gbps) depending on convention. InfiniBand and Ethernet specifications use Gbps; application-level throughput uses GB/s. The text states the convention on first use.
*   Power: Power carries a subscript ($P_{\text{avg}}$, $P_{\text{device}}$, $P_{\text{cluster}}$, $P_{\text{IT}}$); bare $P$ remains parameter count.
*   Latency percentiles: Written p50, p95, and p99 in upright type, inside math as well as in prose.
*   Currency: Dollar amounts use the dollar sign (`$`); unless otherwise noted, dollar-denominated costs are U.S. dollars (USD).
*   Precision:
    *   **FP64**: Double precision (8 bytes)
    *   **FP32**: Single precision (4 bytes)
    *   **TF32**: TensorFloat-32 (19-bit Tensor Core compute mode; inputs and storage remain FP32)
    *   **FP16**: Half precision (2 bytes, standard range)
    *   **BF16**: Brain float (2 bytes, wide dynamic range)
    *   **FP8**: Quarter precision (1 byte, E4M3 or E5M2 format)
    *   **FP4**: 4-bit floating-point format
    *   **INT8**: 8-bit integer (1 byte)
    *   **INT4**: 4-bit integer; lower integer precisions follow the same uppercase `INTn` pattern (for example, INT3, INT2)

### Quick reference: Resolving collisions {#sec-notation-conventions-quick-reference-resolving-collisions-a9cf .unlisted}

Common collision points in distributed ML Systems literature include:

::: {tbl-colwidths="[15,20,25,40]"}

| **Symbol**          | **ML Meaning**    | **Systems Meaning** | **Book Convention**                                    |
|:--------------------|:------------------|:--------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\BatchSize$**    | **Batch Size**    | Bandwidth           | **Batch Size**. Use $\Bandwidth$ for bandwidth.        |
| **$\DatasetSize$**  | **Dataset Size**  | Data Volume         | **Dataset Size**. Use $\DataVolume$ for bytes moved.   |
| **$\LearningRate$** | **Learning Rate** | Efficiency          | **Learning Rate**. Use $\EfficiencyHw$ for efficiency. |
| **$\Loss$**         | **Loss**          | Latency             | **Loss** $(\mathcal{L})$. Use $\Latency$ for latency.  |
| **$\Parameters$**   | **Parameters**    | Peak FLOP/s         | **Parameters**. Use $\PeakRate$ for peak rate.         |

:::

As a general principle, ML conventions take precedence for single letters, while systems concepts get subscripts or multi-letter symbols. This reflects the primary audience (ML practitioners learning systems) and preserves compatibility with the ML literature.

### Additional collision points in distributed execution {#sec-notation-distributed-collisions}

The distributed context introduces further symbol collisions beyond single-device notation:

| **Symbol**             | **ML Meaning**                                        | **Distributed Meaning**                      | **Our Convention**                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|:-----------------------|:------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\NumberOfDevices$** | (none)                                                | Number of Devices                            | **Device Count** in distributed context (accelerators, not host nodes); $N = \AcceleratorCountGpu$.                                                                                                                                    |
| **$M$**                | GEMM dimension; memory root ($\TotalMemoryFootprint$) | Collective Payload                           | **Payload** when bare, outside GEMM shape statements. Memory footprints always carry a subscript.                                                                                                                                      |
| $\lambda$              | Regularization weight                                 | Failure Rate                                 | **Subscript every other use**. Bare $\lambda$ is the per-component failure rate; arrival rate is $\ArrivalRate$.                                                                                                                       |
| $d$, $t$, $p$          | Hidden dimension; time; distribution $p(\cdot)$       | Data-, tensor-, and pipeline-parallel degree | **Core meanings**. Parallelism degrees are $\DataparallelDegreeDp$, $\TensorparallelDegreeTp$, and $\PipelineparallelDegreePp$.                                                                                                        |
| $\tau$                 | Temperature or threshold                              | Checkpoint Interval or Delay                 | **Subscript every distributed use**. Checkpoint intervals are $\CheckpointIntervalCkpt$ and $\OptimalCheckpointIntervalCkpt$; gradient staleness is $\GradientStaleness$.                                                              |
| $\alpha$               | Significance Level                                    | Network Latency                              | **Subscript every other use**. Bare $\alpha$ is $\alpha$-$\beta$ per-message latency; $\ScalingExponentScale$ is the scaling exponent, $\TypeIAndTypeIiErrorRatesSig$ the significance level, and $\alpha_{\text{R}}$ the Rényi order. |
| $\rho$                 | Correlation                                           | Utilization or Ratio                         | **Subscript every other use**. Bare $\rho$ is the communication-computation ratio; $\ServingUtilization$ is serving or queue utilization.                                                                                              |
| $\epsilon$             | Small Constant                                        | Privacy Budget                               | **Subscript every other use**. Bare $\epsilon$ is the privacy budget; $\AdversarialPerturbationBudget$ is the adversarial radius, and stabilizing constants carry their own subscripts.                                                |
| $g$, $G$               | Gradient $\mathbf{g}$                                 | LogGP gaps; GPUs per node                    | **LogGP only** when bare. Gradients are bold $\mathbf{g}$; accelerators per node are $\AcceleratorsPerNode$.                                                                                                                           |
| $K$                    | Top-$K$, key matrix $\mathbf{K}$                      | Attack Steps                                 | **Local when bare**. PGD attack steps are $\AttackStepsPgd$; other counts are defined at use or subscripted ($K_{\text{top}}$).                                                                                                        |
